newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU explains itself to easterners.
newsitem.headline: EU explains itself to easterners.

text.p: The European Union met leaders from 12 aspirant countries on Friday to explain the state of the bloc after the recent summit which finalised a new EU treaty.

Among the main messages the EU was expected to deliver to 10 eastern European countries, Cyprus and Turkey was that internal reforms needed within the EU before eastward expansion can take place have yet to be achieved.

Leaders from 10 eastern European candidates for EU entry -- Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia, Lituania, Romania and Bulgaria -- were at the meeting, along with those from Cyprus and Turkey.

Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and European Commission President Jacques Santer were set to brief the 12 on the outcome of the EU's June 16-17 Amsterdam summit, after voicing concern on Wednesday about the negative impact of the meeting on the EU's plans to expand eastward.

The summit meeting failed to agree the institutional changes considered necessary to prevent paralysis when the EU takes on up to a dozen new members. It agreed that expansion can only take place when those changes have been decided on.
Turkey's EU application has been shunned on human rights grounds and its presence on Friday signalled a renewed will on the part of the EU to make the secular state feel part of the European picture.
